title: Strep throat — Mayo Clinic (summary)
text: Strep throat is a bacterial infection of the throat and tonsils that commonly causes sudden sore throat, pain on swallowing, fever, and sometimes white patches on the tonsils.

title: Common cold — MedlinePlus (summary)
text: The common cold is a mild viral infection that typically causes runny or stuffy nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, and sometimes low-grade fever; symptoms are usually gradual and self-limiting.

title: Influenza (Flu) — Mayo Clinic (summary)
text: Influenza is a viral respiratory illness that often causes sudden high fever, chills, muscle aches, cough, sore throat, headache, and profound fatigue.

title: COVID-19 — WHO (brief)
text: COVID-19 is caused by SARS-CoV-2 and commonly presents with fever, dry cough, fatigue, and may include loss of smell or taste; severe cases can cause difficulty breathing.

title: Gastroenteritis — Cleveland Clinic (summary)
text: Gastroenteritis (stomach flu) causes inflammation of the stomach and intestines, leading to nausea, vomiting, abdominal cramps, and diarrhea, often developing over hours to days.

title: Pneumonia — NIH (summary)
text: Pneumonia is an infection of the lungs that causes cough (often productive), fever, chest pain with breathing, rapid breathing, and shortness of breath; severity varies by cause and patient.

title: Allergic rhinitis — AAFA (summary)
source: Asthma and Allergy Foundation of America
text: Allergic rhinitis (hay fever) produces sneezing, nasal congestion, runny nose, itchy eyes and throat, often triggered by pollen, dust, or pet dander and worsened seasonally.

title: Urinary tract infection — Mayo Clinic (summary)
text: A urinary tract infection commonly causes a frequent urge to urinate, pain or burning during urination, cloudy or strong-smelling urine, and sometimes lower abdominal pain or fever.

title: Appendicitis — NIH (summary)
text: Appendicitis typically causes sudden onset of abdominal pain (often starting near the navel and moving to the lower right), loss of appetite, nausea, and sometimes fever; it often requires urgent evaluation.

title: Migraine — NIH (summary)
text: Migraine is a neurological headache disorder characterized by moderate to severe throbbing head pain, often one-sided, and may include nausea, vomiting, and sensitivity to light or sound.

title: Severe bleeding / hemorrhage (triage note)
text: Significant uncontrolled bleeding, fainting, or signs of shock (pale skin, rapid pulse) indicate a medical emergency and require immediate emergency care.

title: Dehydration — CDC (summary)
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
text: Dehydration can result from vomiting or diarrhea and causes dizziness, decreased urination, dry mouth, and weakness; severe dehydration is an emergency, especially in children and older adults.

title: Asthma — Mayo Clinic (summary)
text: Asthma is a chronic condition causing inflammation and narrowing of the airways, leading to recurrent episodes of wheezing, chest tightness, coughing, and shortness of breath.

title: Concussion — NINDS (summary)
source: National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NINDS)
text: A concussion is a traumatic brain injury often caused by a blow to the head, resulting in symptoms like headache, confusion, dizziness, nausea, and sensitivity to light or noise.

title: Infectious mononucleosis (Mono) — MedlinePlus (summary)
text: Often called 'mono,' this viral infection typically causes profound fatigue, fever, sore throat, and swollen lymph nodes, primarily in the neck and armpits.

title: Meningitis — CDC (summary)
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
text: Meningitis is an inflammation of the membranes surrounding the brain and spinal cord, presenting with a classic triad of high fever, severe headache, and neck stiffness, and often requiring urgent medical attention.

title: Angina (Chest Pain) — Cleveland Clinic (summary)
text: Angina is chest pain or discomfort caused by reduced blood flow to the heart muscle, often described as squeezing, pressure, or heaviness, and may radiate to the jaw or arm; new or worsening angina is a medical emergency.

title: Tendinitis — NIH (summary)
text: Tendinitis is an inflammation of a tendon, a thick cord that attaches muscle to bone, often causing pain, tenderness, and mild swelling near a joint (like the elbow, shoulder, or heel), usually triggered by repetitive motion.

title: Hypoglycemia (Low Blood Sugar) — Mayo Clinic (summary)
text: Hypoglycemia is a condition where the blood sugar level is dangerously low. Symptoms can include shaking, sweating, heart palpitations, confusion, hunger, and sometimes fainting or seizures.

title: Shingles — CDC (summary)
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
text: Shingles is a viral infection that causes a painful rash, typically presenting as a stripe of blisters that wraps around one side of the body or face, often preceded by pain or tingling in the area.

title: Conjunctivitis (Pink Eye) — AAO (summary)
text: Conjunctivitis, or pink eye, is an inflammation of the clear membrane lining the eyelid and eyeball, making the eyes look red or pink, often accompanied by itching, burning, and discharge that can crust over the lashes.

title: Cholecystitis (Gallbladder Inflammation) — Mayo Clinic (summary)
text: Cholecystitis is inflammation of the gallbladder, often caused by gallstones, leading to sudden, severe pain in the upper right or center abdomen, which may spread to the right shoulder or back, accompanied by nausea or vomiting.

title: Kidney Stones — NIH (summary)
text: Kidney stones are hard deposits that form in the kidneys and can cause severe, fluctuating pain (colic) in the side and back, below the ribs, often radiating to the lower abdomen or groin, accompanied by painful urination or blood in urine.

title: Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD) — MedlinePlus (summary)
text: Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD) is characterized by chronic, excessive worry about everyday events, accompanied by physical symptoms like restlessness, muscle tension, difficulty concentrating, and sleep disturbance.

title: Pertussis (Whooping Cough) — CDC (summary)
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
text: Pertussis, or whooping cough, is a highly contagious bacterial disease causing uncontrollable, violent coughing that often makes it hard to breathe, followed by a characteristic 'whooping' sound when inhaling.

title: Sciatica — Mayo Clinic (summary)
text: Sciatica refers to pain that radiates along the path of the sciatic nerve, typically from the lower back through the hips and buttocks and down one leg, often described as a searing or shooting pain, sometimes accompanied by numbness or weakness.

title: Stroke (Triage Note)
text: A stroke occurs when blood flow to a part of the brain is stopped. Symptoms often come on suddenly and include face drooping, arm weakness, and speech difficulty, requiring immediate emergency response.

title: Dengue Fever — CDC (summary)
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
text: Dengue fever, a mosquito-borne illness, is characterized by sudden, high fever, severe headache, severe pain behind the eyes, and intense joint and muscle pain, often called 'break-bone fever,' along with fatigue.

title: Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA) — Mayo Clinic (summary)
text: Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA) is an autoimmune disorder causing chronic inflammation of the joints, leading to pain, swelling, stiffness (especially in the morning), fatigue, and occasionally a low-grade fever.

title: Zika Virus — CDC (summary)
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
text: Zika is a virus spread primarily by mosquitoes, usually causing mild, generalized symptoms including fever, rash, joint pain, muscle pain, and conjunctivitis (red eyes); symptoms typically last for several days to a week.

title: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (Lupus) — Mayo Clinic (summary)
text: Lupus is a chronic autoimmune disease that can affect multiple systems, commonly presenting with joint pain, skin rash (often butterfly-shaped across the face), unexplained fever, and persistent, overwhelming fatigue.

title: Acute Bronchitis — MedlinePlus (summary)
text: Acute bronchitis is inflammation of the bronchial tubes, often following a cold or flu, causing a persistent cough (sometimes with mucus), chest discomfort, mild fever, body aches, and fatigue.

title: Toothache (Dental Pain) — Mayo Clinic (summary)
text: A toothache is pain in or around a tooth, often caused by decay or infection. Pain can be sharp, throbbing, or worsen with hot/cold; it may be accompanied by swelling in the jaw or face, and sometimes fever if an abscess is present.

title: Fibromyalgia — NIH (summary)
text: Fibromyalgia is a disorder characterized by widespread musculoskeletal pain (including **leg ache** and **body ache**), accompanied by fatigue, sleep disturbances, and cognitive difficulties ('fibro fog').

title: Lyme Disease — Mayo Clinic (summary)
text: Lyme disease is a tick-borne bacterial infection. Early symptoms include a characteristic bull's-eye rash (erythema migrans), fever, chills, **body aches**, and fatigue.

title: Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) — CDC (summary)
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
text: Ebola is a rare but severe and often fatal disease. Early symptoms include sudden high fever, severe headache, muscle pain, weakness, and fatigue, followed by vomiting, diarrhea, and sometimes unexplained bleeding.

title: Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (ME/CFS) — NIH (summary)
text: ME/CFS is a complex, long-term illness characterized by extreme **tiredness** and **fatigue** that worsens with physical or mental activity and is not relieved by rest, often accompanied by widespread pain and sleep issues.
